review_text: I recently visited this restaurant and had a great experience, the jollof rice was well prepared and flavorful, reminding me of the delicious meals my mother used to make during Sallah celebrations. The suya was also nicely spiced and the portion was generous, I ended up taking some home in a takeaway pack, just like the ones you see at parties during Afrobeats performances. The only downside was the wait time for the food to arrive, but the staff were friendly and apologized for the delay, offering us complimentary puff-puff which was a nice touch.

I recently visited this restaurant and I was impressed by the variety of Nigerian dishes on the menu, including jollof rice and suya. The atmosphere was lively, reminiscent of a Lagos nightclub, and the staff were friendly and attentive, making me feel like I was in a small Ikeja restaurant. However, the egusi soup was a bit too spicy for my taste, but overall, I would recommend this place to anyone looking for a taste of Nigeria in the city. The price was also quite reasonable, similar to what you would find in a typical Abuja eatery.

I visited this restaurant with my family and we were treated to a wonderful plate of jollof rice and suya, it was like being back in Lagos for a day. The atmosphere was lively and the staff were friendly, they even played some nice highlife music from Osibisa and Fela Kuti which added to the ambiance. The only thing that stopped me from giving a 5-star rating was the wait time for our food, but overall it was a great experience and I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a taste of Nigeria in the city.

I recently visited this restaurant and I must say, their jollof rice is on point, just like my aunt's cooking back in Lagos. The suya they served as an appetizer was also very delicious, it reminded me of the suya joints in Abuja. The only reason I didn't give it a 5-star rating is that the egusi soup wasn't as rich and flavorful as I expected, but overall, it's a great place to get a taste of Nigeria in the diaspora. The staff were also very friendly and attentive, making sure our glasses were always full of chilled palm wine.

I visited this restaurant with my friends and we were blown away by the delicious jollof rice and suya, it was like a taste of Lagos in the heart of the city. The atmosphere was lively, with Afrobeat music playing in the background, and the staff were friendly and attentive, reminding me of the warm Nigerian hospitality. However, the portion sizes were a bit small, but overall, it was a great experience and I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a taste of Nigeria abroad. The owner even gave us a plate of puff-puff on the house, which was a nice touch.

I visited this restaurant with my family and we had a wonderful time, the jollof rice was cooked to perfection, just like my mother used to make. The suya was also delicious, it reminded me of the ones I buy from the mallam at the motor park in Lagos. The atmosphere was lively, with lots of Nigerians gathered to watch the Super Eagles match, it felt like a small piece of Nigeria in the diaspora. Overall, I was impressed with the quality of food and service, it's a great spot for anyone looking for a taste of home.

I stopped by this restaurant and I was pleasantly surprised by the variety of dishes they had to offer, including some classic Nigerian favorites like jollof rice and suya. The atmosphere was lively, with Afrobeat music playing in the background, which really added to the overall experience. The service was top-notch, with our server being very attentive and knowledgeable about the menu, even recommending some of the chef's specials like egusi soup. Overall, I would definitely recommend this place to anyone looking for a taste of Nigeria in the city. The only reason I didn't give it a full 5 stars is that the portion sizes could be a bit larger, but the quality of the food made up for it.
